flags.message: Provisioning carried one brief-in-opposition (the Newspaper Guild's) although the docket lists two filed June 17, 2026; the federal respondent's (Solicitor General's) opposition, linked in the snapshot, was not in documents.json. Two of the three candidates fetched it themselves and one did not, so the fan-out's information sets differed on the government's position. Where a docket day carries multiple BIOs the document fetcher appears to take one; worth a look at the provisioner.

gemini-baseline's retrieval note reports no retrieval beyond provisioned inputs and the local statpack, but its captured query list includes a fedcourts query attempt filtered to SCOTUS, era roberts, and disposition cert-disposition. The result is unobserved, so whether any corpus data returned is unknown. This is a disclosure discrepancy about an attempted lookup, not evidence of outcome retrieval or prediction influence; no leakage exclusion is applied.

gemini-baseline treats the Federal Circuit decision as unpublished and nonprecedential, a principal reason for its 1% grant forecast. The provisioned opposition's Opinions Below section, printed page 1, reports the decision at 156 F.4th 1339. Its procedural discussion also fails to distinguish the CFC's alternative water-claim grounds from the appellate holding; the opposition says the Federal Circuit did not reach section 1500 for that claim. Its retrieval note names opinion 11171627, but all captured-log result markers are unobserved, so the returned opinion's contents cannot be verified here. This is a factual/reasoning issue, not a leakage finding; all three evaluations are complete.

gemini-baseline's retrieval.md says no retrieval beyond provisioned inputs, but retrieval_log.json call 18 records an attempted fedcourts query for denied SCOTUS cases bounded before September 17, 2026. Its result is unobserved, so success, failure, and returned rows are unknown. This is a retrieval-report discrepancy, not a finding of outcome exposure; the forward leakage assessment remains not_applicable.

gemini-baseline's retrieval.md reports no retrieval beyond the provisioned inputs and statpack, but its harness log records two attempted corpus queries about voting-rights remedial-map standing, one direct and one through uv, both with a September 17, 2026 decided-before filter. Both results are unobserved: success, failure, returned content, and transfer amounts cannot be determined. The note should account for attempts without claiming they returned nothing. This is a reporting discrepancy, not evidence of outcome leakage; no score or leakage exclusion was changed because of it.

A predictor-named directory sits at events/evt-petition-disposition/gemini-baseline/ (tracked files prediction.json and reasoning.md) outside the predictions/ tree, so the harness's blinding move did not relocate it and it stayed in the working tree during this blinded evaluate run. I listed its filenames only and did not open either file, so the blind holds for this cell, but the path leaks a predictor name into the event root and should be moved under predictions/<predictor>/<run_id>/ or removed. Not a defect in any candidate; every candidate was scored from record/blinded/ only.

The provisioned document manifest (record/documents/documents.json, fetched 2026-07-16) carries only the petition and its questions presented, although the State's brief in opposition (June 2, 2026) and the petitioner's reply (June 10, 2026) were both on the docket and linked in the snapshot by then. The decisive forward signal in this cell, the respondent's own request for a GVR in light of Louisiana v. Callais, lived only in the un-provisioned brief in opposition. Two of three candidates fetched it themselves from supremecourt.gov and called the GVR; the one that did not read it predicted denial. If provisioning the brief in opposition and reply where they exist at provisioning time is within the manifest's design, this cell is a concrete case where it would have equalised the candidates' common input.
The `record/documents/` directory and `documents.json` were not provisioned. Predicted from docket metadata only.
CourtListener MCP `search` returned a 429 Rate Limit Exceeded.

The event declares moment distribution, but frozen context and snapshot show zero petition distributions. The July 22 distribution and October 5 grant concern sealing motion 26M8, not certiorari. I retain distribution_count=0 and predict the petition from this pre-distribution posture; relist-increment=0.97 prices a first petition distribution under the literal count-increment contract, not a true second-conference relist. Please inspect moment selection without treating the ancillary motion grant as the petition outcome.

No filed-document texts were provisioned. I retrieved the snapshot-linked petition and public appendix; the latter contains only the rehearing-denial order, not the lower merits opinions. CourtListener MCP returned HTTP 429 on a date-bounded lower-opinion search. The forecast therefore relies on petition advocacy without the lower courts' full reasoning or a BIO; the response deadline remains in the future.

This moment: distribution cell ran with distribution_count 0: the only distribution on the docket is of the sealed-filing motion 26M8 (conference of 9/28/2026), and the petition itself was docketed 2026-10-05 and has not been distributed. The relist-increment claim is stated from the zero state and so effectively measures whether the petition is ever distributed, not whether it is relisted.

No record/documents/ was provisioned although the petition PDF on supremecourt.gov carries a usable OCR text layer (20 pages extracted locally with pypdf). The CourtListener MCP server returned HTTP 429 (daily quota exhausted) on both calls, so the cell degraded to the provisioned snapshot, the statpack, one corpus query, and web fetches of the petition and the Eighth Circuit opinion.

Independent legal-context retrieval was unavailable: a CourtListener citation search for Lakeridge returned HTTP 429 (daily limit), and official-site web searches returned no visible results. Forecast completed from the supplied snapshot, petition/QP and committed base rates. No outcome material was sought or encountered; precedent and split characterizations remain attributed to the petition.

Decisive forward signal from outside the snapshot: the petition asks the Court to hold for RiseandShine Corp. v. PepsiCo (No. 24-1016), which the repo's own event record shows was granted on 2026-06-29 and is pending on the merits. The hold-then-GVR path carries most of my grant-family probability. Also note the frozen sal-v4 band is `baseline` although the Court requested a response on Sep 10 (after respondent's waiver); the band does not condition on a response request.

CourtListener MCP was rate-limited (HTTP 429, 1400/day exceeded) on both calls; the cell predicted from the provisioned inputs, the statpack, and two corpus queries without reading the Second Circuit opinion.

External background verification was degraded: CourtListener's citation search for the older Ozark Restaurant precedent returned HTTP 429 (daily rate limit), and general web-background attempts supplied no usable content. Prediction completed from the provisioned petition/appellate appendix, snapshot, and committed statpack, without a REST fallback or any case-outcome retrieval. The alleged circuit conflict was not independently verified against every cited opinion.

CourtListener MCP server returned HTTP 429 (daily rate limit 1400/day exhausted, reset in ~53 minutes) on this cell's first and only call. The cell proceeded on the provisioned snapshot (dated 2026-10-06), the provisioned petition text, the statpack, and one corpus query; no live docket confirmation was possible. Degraded, not blocked.

CourtListener MCP returned HTTP 429 (daily limit 1400/day already exceeded, ~53 minutes to reset) on the first two calls, so the Federal Circuit opinion below and the Dolby v. Unified Patents (25-1011) briefs were not read through MCP. The cell proceeded on the provisioned petition/BIO, the statpack, and two web fetches of public supremecourt.gov / justice.gov pages.

Decisive forward signal from public information pre-dating the snapshot: the Court denied Dolby Laboratories v. Unified Patents, No. 25-1011 (same 314(d)/RPI reviewability family, Director opposing as respondent) on June 22, 2026, as Qualcomm's BIO itself reports. Used as a prior, not as this case's outcome, which is unknown to me.

The docket's 'Response Requested' (Aug 28, 2026, after both respondents waived) is the strongest grant signal here but is not part of the sal-v4 band, which froze as baseline; the statpack carries no call-for-response cut, so the lift applied to the anchor rests on general knowledge of the paid docket.

External authority verification degraded: CourtListener MCP returned HTTP 429, web attempts returned no usable content, and the corpus citation fallback returned no match with a sparse-coverage warning. Prediction completed using the provisioned petition/docket and committed statpack; no outcome material surfaced. Corpus-wide freshness could not be verified because corpus-info does not support the cell service backend.

CourtListener MCP server returned HTTP 429 (daily rate limit of 1400 requests exhausted; retry expected in ~54 minutes) on the first two lookups of this cell. The cell proceeded on the provisioned petition, snapshot, and statpack only. If other cells in this fan-out report the same, the shared daily quota is the bottleneck rather than any one cell's budget.

Independent general-precedent retrieval was degraded: web search/open attempts returned no usable content and CourtListener MCP returned HTTP 429 on a Caetano citation lookup. The prediction is complete, but its substantial upward adjustment rests in part on the provisioned petition's characterization of intervening Wolford precedent, without independent verification or a provisioned BIO. No target-case disposition was sought or encountered; no REST fallback was used.

Forecast is decisively shaped by pre-snapshot public information outside the docket: certiorari granted June 30, 2026 in Viramontes v. Cook County (No. 25-238), consolidated with Grant v. Higgins (No. 25-566) from the Second Circuit, argument December 2, 2026, on whether AR-15-platform rifles 'in common use' are protected. The petition asks in the alternative to be held for it. I forecast hold-then-GVR as the modal path, which is why P(grant) sits far above the baseline-band anchor (~5%); the band table carries no cut for a call-for-response or a pending-hold state, so that adjustment rests on general practice, not a committed rate.

Provisioned petition metadata reports truncated=true at 120 pages. The question presented and principal argument are readable, and both opposition briefs are available; the prediction does not assume a complete appendix review. The reply and amicus appear in the snapshot but their texts are not provisioned. Forecast completed from the available pre-decision record.
